facts.text: Wil Wheaton (Rodney) calls Deep Core 'charming and silly and extremely fun' and says it was the first of two low-budget 'Roger Corman model' knockoffs of big hits he made.
Star Craig Sheffer (Brian Goodman) played Aaron Boone, aka Cabal, in Clive Barker's Nightbreed (1990). He says its monster effects were all practical makeup.
Wil Wheaton says the drilling machine set came apart lengthwise and sat on a homemade gimbal of boards. The cast filmed inside it for about a week.
Wil Wheaton (Rodney Bedecker) says the cramped drilling-vehicle set "looked suspiciously like a shuttlecraft" from a 1990s sci-fi show. He'd know: he was on Star Trek: The Next Generation.
Screenwriter Jim Christopher is credited under the name 'Martin Lazarus.' The story is by Phillip J. Roth, who also produced.
James Russo (government liaison Darryl Simmons) had already worked with director Rodney McDonald on the 1999 action movie Sonic Impact.
Bruce McGill's character is Sam Dalton. McGill earlier played Jack Dalton on the TV series MacGyver, so the name may be a nod to that role.
Bruce McGill (Sam Dalton) is best known as Daniel Simpson "D-Day" Day in John Landis's National Lampoon's Animal House (1978), and as Sheriff Dean Farley in My Cousin Vinny.
To fake the rumbling, director Rodney McDonald said the ride was 'like a tank over a dirt road.' Star Trek vets Terry Farrell and Wil Wheaton asked if that was a 3 on the 'Star Trek shake scale.'
Script Easter eggs: bomb serials "TK421" and "1138" nod to Star Wars (a stormtrooper number Han Solo used) and to George Lucas's first feature, THX 1138 (1971).
Before directing, Rodney McDonald was a first assistant director for Jag Mundhra on The Jigsaw Murders (1989), Night Eyes (1990) and Last Call (1991).
The rock-analysis computer display seen inside the drilling machine was recycled: the same screen shows up in the 2003 sci-fi movie Epoch: Evolution.
Deep Core reached UK viewers first, on Sky MovieMax on December 13, 2000. Paramount released it in the US on video June 26, 2001.
Terry Farrell (Allison Saunders) married Adam Nimoy in 2018, which made her the daughter-in-law of Star Trek's Leonard Nimoy, who'd died in 2015.
Wil Wheaton says someone on set asked for a level 10 shake. Everyone silently declined, because he jokes that only happens when they crash the Enterprise.
Deep Core is linked to earlier earth-cracking B-movies Crack in the World (1965) and Battle Beneath the Earth (1967), and to Armageddon (1998), the hit it was chasing.
Terry Farrell (Allison Saunders) played Jadzia Dax on Star Trek: Deep Space Nine. An asteroid, 26734 Terryfarrell, is named after her.
Harry Van Gorkum (CEO Alan Morrisey) played Nigel Sheffield, Maxwell's dashing brother, on the sitcom The Nanny, where he proposes to Fran Drescher's character.
Wil Wheaton says Deep Core was his take on big disaster movies like Armageddon and The Core. His character Rodney ends up a flaming skeleton after magma hits him.
Story writer and producer Phillip J. Roth also produced Python (2000), the giant-snake movie Wil Wheaton made for the same company, and later Lake Placid 2 (2007).
Paramount picked up Deep Core as its second Armageddon-style acquisition, after Tycus (1999). Matty Budrewicz of The Schlock Pit calls it Armageddon played underground.
Wil Wheaton (Rodney) was Gordie in Stand by Me, then Wesley Crusher on Star Trek: The Next Generation. In Deep Core he's a drilling engineer.
Matty Budrewicz of The Schlock Pit found the effects unusually weak for this type of film. He said the CGI is passable but falls short of Darkdrive (1997).
Paramount put out Deep Core on US video in 2001, then released the big-budget The Core (2003) with a very similar plot. The Schlock Pit notes the overlap.
Deep Core came out three years before The Core (2003), which has a very similar plot: a drilling vehicle sent into Earth's core to set off nukes.
Bruce McGill (Sam Dalton) has played the boss of a time-travel project three times: Quantum Leap, the Bruce Willis-free Timecop (1994) and a Star Trek: Voyager episode.
Harry Van Gorkum (CEO Alan Morrisey) was once cast as the Doctor in the 1996 Doctor Who TV movie. The BBC was unhappy and replaced him with Paul McGann.
Deep Core is set in places like China, Ecuador and the Philippines, but it was filmed around Santa Clarita, California.
The film's reception was poor. IMDb users rated it 2.6/10, AllMovie gave it 1.5 out of 5, and TV Guide gave it 2 out of 5.
After reading the film's dismal ratings, Wil Wheaton (Rodney Bedecker) wrote on his blog that they're "entirely fair, generous, even."
